/-!
# A discrete intermediate value theorem

An integer-valued sequence whose consecutive terms differ by at most `1` attains every
integer value lying between two of its terms. This is the discrete analogue of the
intermediate value theorem for a unit-step walk on `ℤ`.
-/

@[expose] public section

/-- **Discrete intermediate value theorem.** If an integer-valued sequence `f : ℕ → ℤ` has
consecutive terms differing by at most `1`, then it attains every value between `f a` and
`f b`: for `a ≤ b` and `f a ≤ t ≤ f b` there is some index `c ∈ [a, b]` with `f c = t`. -/
theorem Int.exists_eq_of_natAbs_sub_le_one (f : ℕ → ℤ)
    (hf : ∀ n, (f (n + 1) - f n).natAbs ≤ 1) {a b : ℕ} (hab : a ≤ b) {t : ℤ}
    (hta : f a ≤ t) (htb : t ≤ f b) : ∃ c, a ≤ c ∧ c ≤ b ∧ f c = t := by
  induction b, hab using Nat.le_induction with
  | base => exact ⟨a, le_refl a, le_refl a, le_antisymm hta htb⟩
  | succ b hb ih =>
    by_cases h : t ≤ f b
    · obtain ⟨c, hac, hcb, hfc⟩ := ih h
      exact ⟨c, hac, by omega, hfc⟩
    · have hstep := hf b
      exact ⟨b + 1, by omega, le_refl _, by omega⟩

reformulations.difference: The lemma explicitly handles a ≤ b and f a ≤ t ≤ f b, whereas the module's general description of values between two terms allows either ordering of the indices and endpoint values.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: As universally quantified theorem schemes, the formulations are equivalent. For descending endpoint values, apply the ascending formulation to n ↦ -f n and target -t; negation preserves the absolute step bound and the resulting equality is f c = t. Swap the endpoints when their indices are reversed. Conversely, the unordered formulation specializes immediately to the displayed hypotheses. The scratch file proves UpwardIVT ↔ UnorderedIVT by these transformations and instantiates UpwardIVT with the reviewed lemma.
